On 2026-08-23 at 23:05 UTC I received a sextortion email demanding

$2600 USD in bitcoin within 48 hours. No payment was made and no funds

were sent to the address, not even a zero-value transaction.


The sender address displayed in the From header was my own email

address. This is spoofing, not account compromise: SPF and DMARC both

fail at my receiving mail provider, and no anomalous login was found on

the account.




The message claims a trojan was installed on my devices and that webcam

recordings were captured. It contains no attachment, no link and no URL.

It includes no verifiable personal data of any kind, no password, no

device name. The only identifier present is my own email address, copied

from the To field.




Technical observations, from passive analysis only:




The email was not sent from an anonymous server. It was submitted through an authenticated SMTP session (ESMTPSA) on a shared hosting server of a large hosting provider, from a third-party hosting account that appears to have been taken over. The account holder is a legitimate business and is not named here, since all evidence points to them being a victim rather than the author.
The connecting client was a documented residential proxy exit inside an IP broker range. It does not identify the author. Network-level details are available to investigators on request.
The message body was padded with 3192 zero-width characters (U+200B, U+200C, U+200D, U+FEFF) inserted at random positions among 5519 visible characters, to defeat antispam content signatures. Every copy of this email is therefore unique at file level, and file hashes are useless for correlating victims. See the attached screenshot.
The bitcoin address was written in the message with a space inserted in the middle, with an explicit instruction to remove it before sending. This defeats automatic extraction by regex, both in spam filters and in public reporting databases. This is why the address may be underreported.




If you received a similar message, these markers should let you confirm

it belongs to the same campaign:
"Remove the space in the middle of the address when sending"
"There's no point in calling police or any other types of security"
"my Trojan virus controls all processes remotely, just as TeamViewer"
Subject prefix: [INTERNAL] followed by an 8-character hex token
Amount: $2600 USD, deadline: 48 hours, plain text only, no link




SHA-256 of the deobfuscated body (zero-width characters removed, then

whitespace normalised):

eb5a90461fbbb797a211eff2272795fc7e54ede077dcd16231e6394c3244b175




The message explicitly discourages contacting police or telling anyone.

That instruction is part of the modus operandi and is the reason this

report is being filed despite the absence of any financial loss.




A criminal complaint was filed in France. A full technical report with

the complete indicator set is available to investigators on request.

The original raw message is preserved and its hash was anchored via

OpenTimestamps on 2026-08-24.

the sender. They are invisible in any mail client. Note that the line

holding the bitcoin address appears to be the only one left untouched,

which would be consistent with the sender avoiding any risk of

corrupting the payment string.
